sentences.text:
This application coming on for admission this day, the court passed the following:
 ORDER
This is first bail application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. filed on behalf of the applicant for grant of bail, pending the trial.
The applicant is in custody since 16.11.2022 in connection with Crime No.91/2008, registered at P.S.-Naigarhi, District- Rewa (M.P.) for the offence punishable under Sections 363, 366 and 376 of IPC.
As per the prosecution story, on 31.03.2008, more than 16 years old prosecutrix's father lodged an FIR about missing of her daughter.
On 10.06.2008, prosecutrix returned from the Nagpur and stated that she was taken by the Raju Kol at Nagpur and there Raj Kol committed rape upon her.
After investigation, charge sheet was filed long back in the year 2008 but since then applicant could not be arrested.
He has been arrested almost after a period of 14 years.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that applicant has not committed any offence.
He is innocent.
He has been falsely implicated.
Prosecutrix and applicant both belongs to the tribal community.
Prosecutrix at the time of commission of offence was above 16 years of age and had gone with applicant on her own and had stayed with applicant as a wife.
Therefore, it has been prayed that the applicant be released on bail.
On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed the grant of bail.

On a perusal of the certificate issued by the Principal of Government Girls Higher Secondary School,
Naigarhi, it is revealed that at the time of commission of offence prosecutrix was above 16 years and 6 months.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Prosecutrix and applicant both belongs to tribal community and prosecutrix had stayed with applicant at Nagpur for a considerable period.

Undoubtedly, applicant has been arrested after considerable period but looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, I am of the view that it is a case in which further pre-trial detention of the applicant/accused is not warranted.

Consequently,
this first bail application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of bail is allowed.

I t is directed that applicant-Raju Kol be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.
He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.

(DINESH KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE L.R.
